name: Liraglutide
used_for: FDA-labeled as Victoza for glycemic control in adults and children 10 and older with type 2 diabetes and to reduce major cardiovascular events in adults with type 2 diabetes and established cardiovascular disease, and as Saxenda for long-term weight management alongside diet and activity in adults with obesity (or overweight with a weight-related condition) and in children 12 and older with obesity and body weight over 60 kg. The labels advise against using liraglutide products together and carry a boxed warning about thyroid C-cell tumors. Generic liraglutide products are also listed on DailyMed.

entries.text: Victoza (adults): labeled starting dose 0.6 mg subcutaneously once daily for one week (a titration dose not effective for glycemic control), then 1.2 mg daily, with a labeled maximum of 1.8 mg daily after at least one week at 1.2 mg if more glycemic control is needed.
entries.population: Adults with type 2 diabetes per the Victoza label

entries.text: Victoza (children): labeled starting dose 0.6 mg subcutaneously once daily, with increases in 0.6 mg steps after at least one week, up to a labeled maximum of 1.8 mg daily.
entries.population: Patients aged 10 years and older with type 2 diabetes per the Victoza label

entries.text: Saxenda: labeled once-daily subcutaneous schedule of 0.6 mg in week 1, 1.2 mg in week 2, 1.8 mg in week 3, 2.4 mg in week 4, then 3 mg daily from week 5; the label states that for adults 3 mg daily is the recommended dose and lower doses are for titration only. The label says to discontinue if an adult has not lost at least 4% of baseline body weight 16 weeks after starting.
entries.population: Adults with obesity, or overweight with a weight-related condition, per the Saxenda label

administration_guidance.text: The Victoza label states the pen is injected subcutaneously once daily at any time of day, independently of meals, in the abdomen, thigh, or upper arm, and that no adjustment is needed when changing the injection site or timing. The Saxenda label states once-daily injection at any time of day without regard to meals.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: The Victoza and Saxenda labels state that after a missed dose the once-daily regimen is resumed with the next scheduled dose without an extra dose. If more than 3 days have elapsed since the last dose, the labels state treatment is restarted at the initial dosage to reduce gastrointestinal reactions.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: The Victoza label states injection sites within a region should be rotated to reduce the risk of cutaneous amyloidosis, and that when used with insulin the products are given as separate injections and never mixed.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: The Victoza label states a pen is refrigerated (2 to 8 C) before first use and not frozen. After first use it can be kept for 30 days at 15 to 30 C or in the refrigerator, with the cap on, protected from heat and sunlight, with the needle removed and a new needle used each time. The Saxenda label gives the same 30-day in-use rule.
administration_guidance.label: research

side_effects.text: In the Saxenda label's weight-management trials, nausea occurred in 39.3% vs 13.8% with placebo, diarrhea 20.9% vs 9.9%, constipation 19.4% vs 8.5%, vomiting 15.7% vs 3.9%, injection site reactions 13.9% vs 10.5%, and dyspepsia 9.6% vs 2.7%.
side_effects.label: research

side_effects.text: In the Victoza label's type 2 diabetes trials, nausea occurred in 18 to 20% vs 5% with placebo, diarrhea 10 to 12% vs 4%, vomiting 6 to 9% vs 2%, and decreased appetite about 10% vs 1%.
side_effects.label: research

side_effects.text: The Victoza and Saxenda labels carry a boxed warning of thyroid C-cell tumors in rodents (human relevance undetermined) and contraindicate use with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN 2.
side_effects.label: research

side_effects.text: The labels list warnings for acute pancreatitis and acute gallbladder disease, and the Saxenda label reports increased lipase in 5.3% vs 2.2% with placebo.
side_effects.label: research

internet_claims.claim: WebMD patient reviews of Saxenda describe weight losses from a few pounds to dozens of pounds and reduced food cravings for many users, alongside frequent nausea, digestive problems and fatigue; some find side effects hard to tolerate and a few report little effect.

research.summary: FDA-approved DailyMed prescribing information for Victoza (liraglutide) injection (Novo Nordisk), published November 2025.
research.finding: Lists approved uses for type 2 diabetes glycemic control (adults and patients 10 and older) and cardiovascular risk reduction in adults with established cardiovascular disease; once-daily dosing up to 1.8 mg; boxed warning for thyroid C-cell tumors.

research.summary: FDA-approved DailyMed prescribing information for Saxenda (liraglutide) injection (Novo Nordisk), published June 2026.
research.finding: Lists approved use for chronic weight management in adults and in patients 12 and older with obesity and weight over 60 kg, with a 3 mg daily maintenance dose; boxed warning for thyroid C-cell tumors.

research.summary: LEADER: double-blind trial of liraglutide versus placebo in 9,340 adults with type 2 diabetes at high cardiovascular risk, median follow-up 3.8 years (Marso et al., N Engl J Med).
research.finding: The composite of cardiovascular death, nonfatal heart attack or nonfatal stroke occurred in 13.0% with liraglutide versus 14.9% with placebo (hazard ratio 0.87). Gastrointestinal events were the most common reason for stopping. Funded by Novo Nordisk and the NIH.

research.summary: SCALE Obesity and Prediabetes: 56-week double-blind trial of liraglutide 3.0 mg daily versus placebo in 3,731 adults with obesity or overweight with a weight-related condition and without type 2 diabetes (Pi-Sunyer et al., N Engl J Med).
research.finding: Mean weight loss was 8.4 kg with liraglutide versus 2.8 kg with placebo; 63.2% versus 27.1% lost at least 5% of body weight. Nausea and diarrhea were the most common side effects; serious events occurred in 6.2% versus 5.0%. Funded by Novo Nordisk.

research.summary: LEAD-6: 26-week open-label trial of liraglutide 1.8 mg daily versus exenatide 10 mcg twice daily in 464 adults with type 2 diabetes on oral drugs (Buse et al., Lancet).
research.finding: HbA1c fell 1.12% with liraglutide versus 0.79% with exenatide; weight loss was similar (about 3 kg in both). Nausea was less persistent with liraglutide. Open-label design.

research.summary: Ellipse: double-blind trial of liraglutide up to 1.8 mg daily versus placebo in 134 children and adolescents (mean age 14.6) with type 2 diabetes, 52 weeks (Tamborlane et al., N Engl J Med).
research.finding: At 26 weeks HbA1c fell 0.64 points with liraglutide and rose 0.42 with placebo (difference -1.06). Gastrointestinal adverse events were more frequent with liraglutide. Small trial funded by Novo Nordisk.

research.summary: 3-year assessment of SCALE Obesity and Prediabetes: double-blind trial of liraglutide 3.0 mg daily versus placebo in 2,254 adults with prediabetes and obesity or overweight, with diet and activity advice (le Roux et al., Lancet). About half of participants completed 160 weeks.
research.finding: Diabetes was diagnosed on treatment in 2% with liraglutide versus 6% with placebo (hazard ratio 0.21). Weight change at week 160 was -6.1% versus -1.9%. Participants who withdrew were not followed up after stopping. Funded by Novo Nordisk.

research.summary: Pooled post hoc safety analysis of one phase 2 and four phase 3a randomized placebo-controlled trials of liraglutide 3.0 mg in 5,325 people (3,384 liraglutide, 1,941 placebo), including a 12-week off-treatment follow-up in the SCALE trials (O'Neil et al., Diabetes Obes Metab).
research.finding: No neuropsychiatric safety signals were seen at the end of the 12-week off-treatment period to suggest withdrawal or rebound effects (not measured in the SCALE Sleep Apnoea trial).

dose.summary: Victoza starts at 0.6 mg once daily and goes up to 1.2 mg, with a labeled maximum of 1.8 mg. Saxenda steps up weekly from 0.6 mg to 3 mg daily. Nothing was found online that differs from these doses.

cycle_length.summary: Used as long-term treatment. Trials ran 56 weeks to 3 years, and the Saxenda label says to stop if an adult has lost less than 4% of body weight after 16 weeks. No withdrawal effects were seen in the 12 weeks after stopping, but the 3-year trial did not follow people who left. An online pharmacy says weight regain is common after stopping and that tapering is optional.

items.text: The Saxenda label states adults should be evaluated 16 weeks after starting, and treatment stopped if they have not lost at least 4% of baseline body weight.
items.label: research

items.text: The SCALE trial gave liraglutide 3.0 mg daily for 56 weeks, and its 3-year assessment in people with prediabetes kept treatment for up to 160 weeks, with about half of participants completing. People who withdrew were not followed after stopping.
items.label: research

items.text: In a pooled analysis of the SCALE trials, a 12-week off-treatment follow-up found no signs of withdrawal or rebound effects on mood or suicidal thoughts after stopping liraglutide 3.0 mg.
items.label: research

items.text: Bolt Pharmacy, a UK online pharmacy, says Saxenda causes no physical dependence or withdrawal on abrupt stopping, that many patients notice more hunger within days, and that weight regain after stopping is common. It says tapering over 2 to 4 weeks is not medically required but some clinicians and patients prefer it.
items.label: internet

Rotate injection sites, use a new needle each time, and never mix with insulin. Cleveland Clinic's patient page agrees with the label.

mechanism.summary: A long-acting version of the gut hormone GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1). It raises insulin when blood sugar is high, lowers glucagon, slows stomach emptying, and reduces appetite through the brain.

items.text: The Victoza label describes liraglutide as an acylated GLP-1 receptor agonist with 97% sequence similarity to human GLP-1. It raises insulin release when glucose is high, lowers glucagon in a glucose-dependent way, and delays gastric emptying. Its plasma half-life is about 13 hours.
items.label: research

items.text: The Saxenda label states liraglutide reduces body weight by lowering calorie intake through appetite regulation in the brain, and that it is stable against breakdown by enzymes, with a half-life of 13 hours after injection, allowing once-daily dosing.
items.label: research

best_documented_effect.summary: In Saxenda's main trial, about 8 kg average weight loss over 56 weeks versus 3 kg on placebo. In type 2 diabetes, fewer heart attacks, strokes and cardiovascular deaths over several years.

side_effect_groups.summary: Boxed warning for thyroid C-cell tumors in rodents, plus pancreatitis and gallbladder disease.

side_effect_groups.title: Low blood sugar
side_effect_groups.summary: More likely when combined with a sulfonylurea or insulin; uncommon in children without diabetes.

items.text: In the Victoza label's combination trials, low blood sugar needing self-treatment occurred in 7.5% with Victoza plus glimepiride (a sulfonylurea) versus 2.6% with placebo plus glimepiride.
items.label: research

items.text: In the Saxenda label's pediatric trial in patients without type 2 diabetes, clinically significant low blood sugar (below 54 mg/dL) occurred in 1.6% with Saxenda versus 0.8% with placebo.
items.label: research
